title: The scheduler tick cannot learn the tenant of its API key, so ISS-T037WIRE-001 (LKB_TENANT_ID differs from the key's tenant) is only PARTLY closed: tenant-mismatch detection exists but has no production input
area: apps/api (read-only here): GET /meeting-candidates and GET /calendar/upcoming (non-native) responses; auth.ts VerifiedKey.tenantId; packages/meeting-bot schedule-tick.ts
evidence: Responses the tick already fetches: /meeting-candidates -> {candidates:[{_id,messageId,subject,senderEmail,senderDomain,meetingUrl,status,detectedAt,decidedAt,kind,startTime,endTime,recordingUrl,registrationOnly}]}; /calendar/upcoming?discovery=1 -> {meetings:[...]}; none carries a tenant id. Only the native-acquisition shape (?sync=1) echoes tenantId, and the real tick does not use it. GET /keys returns {_id,label,scopes,createdAt,revokedAt} with no tenant id and needs the keys scope. There is no whoami/self route. So with enforcement ON and LKB_TENANT_ID naming another tenant, A's meetings are filtered by B's rules (reproduced by the recorded ISS-T037WIRE-001 case; pinned in join-rules-enforce-preconditions.test.ts).
fix_direction: Add ONE authenticated read-only route returning the caller's tenant (e.g. GET /whoami -> {tenantId}, any scope, tenantId = req.auth.tenantId, validated by isValidTenantId) OR add tenantId to the /meeting-candidates response body. Then in buildRealScheduleTickDeps fetch it once per tick and pass it as joinRulesKeyTenantId (the compare, the tenant-mismatch reason and both policy behaviours already exist and are tested; an unreachable/invalid answer must be treated as mismatch when enforcing). Needed before an enabling value is set; severity HIGH at enablement.
regression_check: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-enforce-preconditions.test.ts (key tenant known: mismatch; production shape: residual pinned)
verified_by: checker verdict: cycle 0 PASS (source scope; deployment/enablement gates not discharged)

title: The maker's claim that no existing API response carries the key's tenant is wrong: GET /webinar-operations already returns the header X-LKB-Tenant = req.auth.tenantId, and the sibling webinar pipeline already uses it for exactly this check; ISS-WIREPRE-001's fix_direction (add a whoami route or a body field) is therefore not needed
evidence: brain.ts: router.get('/webinar-operations', requireScope('sessions'), ...) sets res.setHeader('X-LKB-Tenant', req.auth!.tenantId). run-pipeline-deps.mjs validateTenant fetches ${api}/webinar-operations with the same LKB_API_KEY and throws 'Connected API owner does not match the configured capture lane' unless response.headers.get('x-lkb-tenant') === env.LKB_TENANT_ID. So a key-authoritative tenant signal exists today with no API change; the manifest and ISS-WIREPRE-001 say 'no existing response carries it ... no whoami route'. (Body-level the claim holds: /meeting-candidates, /calendar/upcoming and /keys bodies carry no tenant id. Not derivable from candidate ids or the rules store directory either.)
fix_direction: Feed joinRulesKeyTenantId from a once-per-tick GET /webinar-operations header (copy the validateTenant pattern; redirect:'error', short timeout, cancel the body); header absent, request failed or non-matching = mismatch when enforcing. Open question for the unit: the tick's LKB_API_KEY needs the 'sessions' scope; if it lacks it, either grant it or add the whoami route. Alternative design that removes the problem: have the tick read rules through the key-scoped GET /calendar/join-rules instead of a local file keyed by LKB_TENANT_ID. Severity of the whole tenant condition remains HIGH at enablement (ISS-T037WIRE-001).
